ui.ray: Ray, the Fabricator stingray. Select to pet him.

rayfin.classes: Rayfin turns TypeScript classes into a database, APIs and a type-safe client.
rayfin.decorators: Your data model is plain TypeScript. Decorators like @text, @int and @date describe each field.
rayfin.rayfinUp: One command, rayfin up, publishes the whole app to Microsoft Fabric.
rayfin.boundary: Rayfin apps run on Microsoft Fabric, inside your organization’s boundary.
rayfin.signIn: Sign-in comes built in: Rayfin apps sign people in with Microsoft Entra ID.
rayfin.rowLevelSecurity: A policy on @authenticated can show each person only their own rows. Row-level security, in one line.
rayfin.relations: @one and @many link entities, so a customer can have many orders.
rayfin.queries: Rayfin queries are type-safe chains: select, where, orderBy, then execute.
rayfin.aggregates: Need totals? groupBy() and aggregate() handle sums, averages and counts.
rayfin.validators: Rayfin can generate a validator from an entity, so a form can check input before it’s saved.
rayfin.connectors: Connectors read data that already lives in Fabric: warehouses, SQL databases, semantic models and KQL databases.
rayfin.dax: With a connector, your app can run DAX against a Fabric semantic model.
rayfin.functions: Functions run server-side TypeScript next to your data. Heads up: they aren’t in every Fabric region yet.
rayfin.secrets: Functions can call outside APIs with keys kept as secrets, so the keys never sit in your code.
rayfin.versions: Every @microsoft/rayfin-* package shares one version number, so upgrades move in lockstep.
rayfin.universalApp: New apps start from Rayfin’s Universal App. It starts small and grows into whatever you describe.
rayfin.hosting: Rayfin hosts your frontend too. The built app is served from Fabric, next to its data.
rayfin.files: Rayfin apps can keep files too, like photos and receipts, in their own file storage.
rayfin.typeScript: Rayfin is TypeScript all the way down: data model, client code and app logic.
rayfin.docs: Rayfin’s docs are written for agents too. Add .md to any page on rayfin.ai to get it as Markdown.

tip.describe: Describe what you want in plain English. Copilot writes the code, and I cheer.
tip.design: In the preview, Design lets you point at anything and ask for a change.
tip.history: Every change is kept. Code → History can restore an earlier version.
tip.advisor: The Advisor grades your app’s health, and every finding comes with a one-click fix.
tip.blueprint: Blueprint shows how your app is put together, data model included.
tip.secrets: An API key for a function? Add it in Code → Secrets, so it never sits in your code.
tip.publish: Publishing puts your app on Microsoft Fabric, where people in your organization can open it.
tip.autoPublish: Publish after each chat turn decides whether every change goes to Fabric right away.
tip.share: Once your app is published, Share lets people in your organization open it.
tip.help: Stuck later? Select Help in the status bar, and I’ll dig through the logs with you.

ray.cartilage: Rays are cousins of sharks. Our skeletons are cartilage, not bone.
ray.rayFinned: Plot twist: despite the name, rays aren’t ray-finned fish. We’re closer to sharks.
ray.eyes: A stingray’s eyes are on top and its mouth is underneath, so it can watch while it eats.
ray.electric: Rays can sense the faint electric fields of prey hiding in the sand.
ray.fever: A group of stingrays is called a fever. I’m not making that up.
ray.mantaBrain: Manta rays have the biggest brains of any fish.
ray.mantaSpan: The giant manta ray can grow about 7 meters from wingtip to wingtip.
